messages:
ada: Quick follow-up from today's multi-region RFC — question about KV cache ownership during active/active failover when data residency blocks cross-region key export. If a tenant is resident in eu-west, but we failover to us-west for capacity reasons, how do we avoid decrypting their KV entries with a US KMS key?

mario: short answer: we shouldn't. Residency says keys must stay in-region. Options: 1) keep serving from eu nodes only (higher latency), 2) replicate encrypted blobs and keep keys in-region + remote decryption proxy, or 3) fallback to a compatible model variant that doesn't need per-tenant KV.

julie: option 2 implies a decryption proxy call across regions which likely breaks residency too unless proxy runs in eu. Also adds latency and availability coupling.

kevin: can we do a hybrid: replicate KV blobs (ciphertext) to nearby region but never export keys. If failover happens, route read requests back to eu KMS via a signed short-lived RPC that only returns transient plaintext or ephemeral derived material? That still touches eu KMS but traffic crosses regions — legal might object.

ada: @kevin that's basically a remote-unseal pattern. Works technically if allowed, but we need explicit product/legal signoff. Also SLO hit could be severe.

mario: another idea: keep a small fenced eu-only control-plane that holds decryption capability and forwards only tokens/answers (not plaintext) — like an unbundled crypto enclave. If us-west nodes need to serve, they call the eu enclave for the final tokenization/expansion step. Latency + cost tradeoff.

julie: we must enumerate threat model and compliance constraints before choosing. For example: does GDPR/local data residency allow ciphertext replication if keys never leave region? Some countries accept that, some don’t. Need legal input per geography.

sre-bot: incident note: last cross-region KMS proxy experiment (2025-11-02) increased P95 by 230ms and produced transient KMS latency spikes.

kevin: pragmatic proposal for RFC follow-up: 3 tracks — A) Strict residency: refuse cross-region failover for resident tenants (fail closed or degraded mode). B) Remote-unseal: replicate ciphertext + keep KMS in origin region + proxy decryption (only if legal ok). C) Model-level fallback: route to lightweight model variant or cached responses that don't require KV decryption.

ad a: we should also add a short compatibility shim in the runtime: flag `tenant.residency_policy = { allow_cross_failover: bool, fail_mode: enum }` so customers can opt-in/out. Default: false for regulated tenants.

mario: action items: 1) Julie to get legal on residency vs ciphertext replication (ETA 48h). 2) Kevin to sketch remote-unseal latency budget and retry/backoff model (ETA 72h). 3) Ops to produce cost delta for running eu enclave + cross-region egress (SLO impact + $). 4) Add runtime flag RFC patch (me + ada) — will propose changes in the multi-region RFC doc.

julie: noted, I'll ping legal and post findings here.

kevin: I'll drop a micro-benchmark snippet in the RFC thread. sample command: 
```bash
# measures unseal p95 to eu KMS proxy
curl -sS -X POST https://unseal-proxy.internal/eu/unseal -d '{"blob":"..."}' | jq -r '.latency'
```

ada: thanks. For rollout: prefer canary resident tenants only, then widen. Also add telemetry: unseal_count, unseal_fail_rate, cross_region_calls.

mario: agreed. I'll open a short RFC follow-up PR summarizing the 3 tracks + runtime flag tonight. Please leave comments there so we have a single source of truth.

julie: thanks all. If legal says ciphertext replication is fine we can prioritize remote-unseal; otherwise strict residency + model fallback is our default plan.

kevin: tagging for follow-up: @ada @mario @julie. I'll post numbers in the RFC PR.

sre-bot: deploy-bot: multi-region/rfc-followup branch built: sha=abc123 - canary tests pending.
